$doc: SSOT for the maximum defensible security posture (ADR-CORE-039, ADR-APP-033). Project-owned: every project has a different toolchain, so this is never pinned and never delivered by governance:update. The gate scripts/lib/security-posture-gate.mjs (loaded from eslint.config.mjs) enforces it: every canonical category is declared; every 'enabled' safety is actually wired into check:all (or its config stays set); every 'deferred' safety carries a non-empty 'why'; the key linters keep their teeth. To change the posture you change THIS file — and the gate keeps you honest.

js-advisory-scan.note: npm audit on production deps, --audit-level=high. Rust deps were scanned; JS deps were not — this closes that gap.

secret-scan.note: secretlint over the working tree; eslint-plugin-no-secrets in the lint run as a second layer.

sast.note: eslint-plugin-security (recommended) on src and the tooling scripts.

dead-code.note: unused files/exports/deps are a red build.

rust-lint-strict.note: clippy -D warnings PLUS [lints.clippy] undocumented_unsafe_blocks = deny — the gate verifies the Cargo.toml setting directly, so every unsafe block must justify itself.

ts-lint-strict.note: eslint --max-warnings 0 PLUS tsconfig strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess — the gate verifies the tsconfig setting directly.

compiler-hardening.note: [profile.release] overflow-checks = true in src-tauri/Cargo.toml — the gate verifies it directly (no check:all step exercises the release profile). An integer overflow panics (and is caught by ADR-APP-032) instead of wrapping silently.

dep-pinning.note: npm exact versions + committed package-lock.json / Cargo.lock; --locked on cargo build/test; cargo-deny 'sources' check.

rust-supply-chain-vet.why: cargo-vet needs audits or exemptions for ~450 transitive crates; it is not clean by any reasonable bar even after importing Mozilla/Google audit sets. Revisit if the trust base shrinks or a maintained audit set covers most of the tree.

sast-semgrep.why: Semgrep CLI needs a curated, pinned ruleset to be net-positive; with --config=auto it is high-noise on day one and trains suppression. eslint-plugin-security covers the JS SAST surface today. Revisit with a vetted ruleset.

sast-codeql.why: CodeQL's normal GitHub-Action-on-push model contradicts this stack's release-only CI (no push/PR CI, ADR-APP-103/rule:automation). A local CLI-only run is nonstandard; semgrep is the better local fit if a dedicated SAST is added.

secret-scan-history.why: secretlint and eslint-no-secrets scan the working tree; gitleaks (git history) adds a Go binary to the local gate. Working-tree coverage holds now; a history scan is a one-time/CI concern, not a per-commit gate.

sbom.why: An SBOM is a release artifact, not a per-commit pass/fail check; cargo-cyclonedx + cyclonedx-npm add binary friction to the local gate for no gate semantics. It belongs in the release build (release.yml) and is tracked there, not here.

fuzzing.why: ADR-CORE-039 scopes fuzzing to code that parses UNTRUSTED input; none exists yet — only local, self-produced settings.json and crash markers are deserialized. Add a cargo-fuzz harness when a network-facing or externally-supplied format is parsed.

cargo-exact-pins.note: Every direct dependency in src-tauri/Cargo.toml carries an exact '=' requirement (the gate verifies it); a `cargo update` cannot silently move a direct dep off the committed Cargo.lock.

linker-hardening.note: .cargo/config.toml: Windows Control Flow Guard, Linux full RELRO + BIND_NOW (the gate verifies rustflags are set). macOS stays at the toolchain default (PIE + hardened runtime) — not verifiable on this machine, so it surfaces in the release build per rule:automation.
